result:
## One thing to know first

This worktree is checked out at `a3b3c3685bc`, which is **148 commits before the stable chunk build existed** — `posthog/stable_chunks.py`, `common/esbuilder/stableChunkNames.mjs` and the `?stable_chunks=1` opt-in were all absent, so there was nothing to put behind a flag. To restore the state your request describes, I cherry-picked the prerequisite as its own commit (`62e2c521798`, "serve stable chunk names behind an opt-in", original author preserved, with a `cherry picked from` trailer). My change is the **uncommitted diff on top of it** — `git diff` shows exactly my work.

## What I changed

**`posthog/stable_chunks.py`** — the decision now has three inputs instead of one:

- `stable_chunks_choice(request) -> bool | None` replaces `stable_chunks_opted_in`. It returns the browser's own choice (query param, else cookie) or `None` when the browser has not chosen. Previously "no choice" and "chose off" were the same answer, which is exactly the distinction the flag needs.
- `serves_stable_chunks(request, feature_flags)` — an explicit choice wins; otherwise an anonymous request is never enrolled, and a logged-in request is served the stable build when `stable-chunk-build` (`STABLE_CHUNKS_FEATURE_FLAG`) is `True`.
- `persist_stable_chunks_choice` now **stores** `?stable_chunks=0` as a cookie rather than deleting the cookie. Without this the escape hatch is one-shot: the flag re-enrolls the browser on the very next page load. Both directions persist for 30 days.

**`posthog/utils.py:749`** — passes the flags already evaluated for this request (`posthog_bootstrap["featureFlags"]`, from the existing `get_all_flags` call a few lines above) into `stable_chunks_for_request`. Reading the decision from that set rather than a second evaluation call costs nothing extra and, more importantly, guarantees the build a user is served matches the `$feature/stable-chunk-build` property their events carry — which is what makes the LCP breakdown trustworthy. It also gives the anonymous exclusion for free, since that dict only exists for a logged-in user.

## Tests

- `test_stable_chunks.py`: folded the opt-in cases into `test_who_is_served_the_stable_build`, testing through `serves_stable_chunks` (the decision, not the cookie parser) across 8 cases — param and cookie beating the flag in both directions, the flag deciding when the browser hasn't chosen, no flags evaluated, and anonymous with the flag on. Stays on `SimpleTestCase` (no DB) by stubbing `request.user`. Updated the persistence cases for the stored opt-out.
- `test_get_context_for_template.py`: added a case to the import-map test for "no param, logged in, flag on" → stable build with the authenticated preload chain. That's the wiring regression the unit test can't catch: if the evaluated flags stop being passed into `stable_chunks_for_request`, every flagged user silently gets the current build and the experiment reads as no-effect.

Per your instruction I didn't run the suite; `ruff` isn't installed in this worktree, so I checked syntax and the 120-char limit by hand.

## What's left outside the code

The flag `stable-chunk-build` has to be created at 50% rollout with local evaluation available (the server reads it from the locally-evaluated flag set, so a flag that can't be evaluated locally reads as off — fail-safe, but a silent 0% rollout). One measurement caveat: a user who forces the build on with the query param while their flag says `false` lands in the control group's LCP numbers with the treatment build. Fine for a handful of internal force-ons, worth excluding by cohort if it spreads.
